title: Customer Churn Analysis — Verified Findings Report
executive_summary: Across 749 customers, 37.65% have churned and the average monthly fee is $42.11. Churn barely differs by plan or signup cohort, but contract type matters greatly: Monthly customers churn at 48.32% versus 21.85% for Annual (+121.11%). A well-defined at-risk segment of 100 customers with 5+ support tickets and satisfaction ≤2 churns at 71.00%. Lifetime value rises sharply with plan tier — Premium averages $1,816.78, about 3.92× Basic's $463.46. Priorities: move Monthly customers to Annual contracts and intervene early with the high-ticket, low-satisfaction segment.

key_findings.statement: The cleaned dataset contains 749 customers. The overall churn rate is 37.65% and the average monthly fee is $42.11.
Churn differs little by plan: Basic 38.87%, Standard 36.68% and Premium 36.60% — a spread of only 2.27 percentage points between the highest (Basic) and lowest (Premium).
Churn is broadly flat across signup cohorts: 2022 is lowest at 36.74% and 2024 highest at 39.83% (a range of 3.09 percentage points), with 2021 at 38.02% and 2023 at 37.05%.
Contract type is the strongest churn differentiator: Monthly customers churn at 48.32% versus 21.85% for Annual — 26.47 percentage points more, a relative increase of 121.11%.
100 customers (13.35% of the base) have 5+ support tickets and a satisfaction score of 2 or less; 71.00% of them churned — about 1.89× the overall churn rate of 37.65%.
Typical tenure is around two years: mean 20.81 months, median 19.00 months, standard deviation 13.25 months. Average satisfaction is 3.42, and 27 customers have no satisfaction score recorded.
Lifetime value rises steeply with plan tier: Basic $463.46, Standard $868.83 and Premium $1,816.78 — Premium is 292.01% higher than Basic, roughly 3.92× the value.

limitations: Findings are descriptive only; no statistical significance tests were run, so the small plan and cohort differences (a few percentage points) may reflect random variation.
Associations (e.g., contract type, support tickets, satisfaction) are correlational and do not prove causation.
27 customers lack a satisfaction score and are excluded from satisfaction-based metrics, which could bias the at-risk segment definition.
Signup cohorts have unequal observation windows: 2024 customers have had less time to churn, yet already show the highest churn rate.
Lifetime value reflects recorded revenue only; cost and margin data were not available, so profitability by plan is unknown.
conclusion: Retention efforts should prioritise converting Monthly customers to Annual contracts (48.32% vs 21.85% churn) and proactive outreach to the 100-customer at-risk segment, which churns at 71.00%. Plan tier and cohort effects on churn are minor, but because Premium customers deliver $1,816.78 in average lifetime value, protecting and growing that tier offers the largest revenue payoff.
